Subject: Performance SLO follow-up  context window & latency impact

Hi John / Emily 

Thanks again for the call earlier  really appreciate the clear goals you set around latency and availability. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

- Goals you shared: p95 latency <= 800ms for synchronous calls, target throughput ~20 QPS, concurrency typical spikes up to 8-12, streaming for long responses is preferred to improve perceived latency.
- Key constraints: many requests will include ~6-8k tokens of historical context (customer transcripts + metadata) and expected output typically 256-1024 tokens depending on the workflow.
- Risks we flagged: larger context windows increase memory/compute footprint and can push tail latency up; batching and concurrency tradeoffs will affect p95.

Next steps I propose:
1) Rishi to provide initial latency/throughput estimates for 4k vs 8k context windows across the model variants we discussed and recommended streaming behavior.
2) We’ll share an estimate spreadsheet (attached) and a draft mutual action plan  if that looks good we’ll schedule a short PoC to run a representative workload.
3) Security/Procurement: Emily, if you can share the internal timeline we’ll align the PoC window.

Attachments: finco_mvp_perf_estimates.xlsx (initial estimate), mvp-mutual-action-plan.docx (MVP MAM).

I’ll leave the technical load to Rishi  thanks team.

Marissa  thanks for the recap. Confirming a couple clarifications before Rishi dives in: 

1) Our p95 target of 800ms is for end-to-end time to first meaningful token or full response? We're flexible but want to be clear  perceived latency (time to first token) matters because our UI streams incremental answers.
2) The 20 QPS requirement is steady-state for our production; peak concurrency during campaigns could reach 12-15 concurrent requests.
3) On context: the 6-8k token figure is accurate for our most-used flows (search + long conversation history). Worst case may include up to 10k tokens in rare sessions.

If you can outline whether the SLO is achievable for (a) synchronous full-response, and (b) streaming-first-token scenario for 8k context at 20 QPS, that will help our procurement/architects. Also, what tradeoffs would you recommend (quantization, model sizing, dedicated capacity)?

Thanks  happy to hop on a short call if easier.

John

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: John Park <john.park@finco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 07 Apr 2027 15:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO follow-up  context window & latency impact

John  thanks for the clear questions. Below are our initial, conservative estimates and the recommended levers. These are based on our Dedicated runtime with a production-optimized LLM (we can run a quick PoC on your sample traffic to validate):

Short answers up front:
- Synchronous full-response SLO (p95 <= 800ms): generally achievable for inputs up to ~4k tokens with optimized model (medium-sized variant) at moderate concurrency (<=4). For 8k token inputs, synchronous p95 <= 800ms is unlikely on a single GPU at 20 QPS without aggressive sharding/replication.
- Streaming-first-token SLO (time to first token): much more achievable  we can often deliver first token within 150-300ms even for larger context windows by prioritizing KV prefetch and early decoding.

Estimates (single GPU config / dedicated pool / conservative):
- 2k input + 256 output: p50 ~120ms, p95 ~300ms, throughput ~60 QPS (concurrency 8).
- 4k input + 512 output: p50 ~180ms, p95 ~450ms, throughput ~30-40 QPS (concurrency 6-8).
- 8k input + 512 output: p50 ~320ms, p95 ~900ms, throughput ~12-18 QPS (concurrency 4-6).
- 10k input + 1k output: p50 ~480ms, p95 >1200ms (not within your 800ms SLO without horizontal scaling).

Notes on what drives these numbers:
- Context window scaling: memory and KV cache misses increase with larger context; CPU/GPU memory copies and attention computation increase roughly quadratically with sequence length slices, so latency grows non-linearly.
- Concurrency and batching: batching increases throughput but adds wait time per request; at your target 20 QPS, we'd size the pool (replicas + autoscale) to keep batching small to preserve p95.
- Streaming helps perceived latency: by starting decoding as soon as prefix tokens are processed, the time to first token is dominated by model startup and KV prefetch (~150-350ms depending on context), while total time to full response remains similar.

Recommended levers for FinCo to meet p95 <=800ms for most traffic:
1) Enable streaming-first-token UX for end-users (best bang-for-buck).
2) Use dedicated capacity with 2-3 replicas (depends on traffic shaping) to reduce queuing and keep batching tight.
3) Quantization (8-bit or mixed) can reduce latency by ~10-25% in many models  we’ll validate on your model.
4) For very large contexts (>8k) consider a hybrid approach: fetch dense embeddings for older history and keep recent 2-3k tokens in full context. This typically preserves quality while lowering compute.

Next steps I suggest:
- We run a short PoC (48-72 hours) with a small set of representative requests. Rishi + Neha to provision a dedicated test pool, run workload, and share actual p50/p95 plots.
- Share workload sample (John) and any redlines on data retention or tokens that cannot be sent.

I’ll attach a spreadsheet with the above numbers broken down and a simple cost estimate per 1M tokens.

Cheers,
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

Rishi  this is helpful, thanks. A couple follow-ups: 

- Streaming-first-token is our preferred UX. If time to first token is typically ~200-300ms for 8k context, that’s acceptable. What does partial output streaming look like for longer responses (e.g., 1k tokens)? Will you stream every N tokens or is it chunked by sentence?
- For the hybrid approach (embeddings for older history), do you have any guidance on how to select which segments to compress/replace? We have some telemetry on recency importance that we can share.
- We’re fine running a 72-hour PoC. We can provide an anonymized sample batch of ~50k tokens per minute peak traffic for the PoC window. Please propose start dates.

Also, can you confirm the data handling for the PoC (retention window, logs access for us)? Emily — FYI for procurement.

John

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: John Park <john.park@finco.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@finco.com>
Date: Wed, 07 Apr 2027 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO follow-up  context window & latency impact

John  great, glad we’re aligned. Quick answers and next steps: 

- Streaming behavior: we stream tokens as they’re produced; by default we send partial chunks every ~64 tokens (configurable). For longer outputs (1k tokens) that means the UI will receive incremental chunks shortly after the first token; time to first token remains the key metric for perceived latency. We can tune chunk size during the PoC.
- Hybrid history strategy: Rishi and Neha will help define heuristics (recency, user signals, embedding similarity)  happy to take a short telemetry sample from you and propose a compression policy.
- PoC: proposed window is Mon Apr 12 — Wed Apr 14 (72 hrs). Rishi/Neha will provision a dedicated test pool and share onboarding steps and a short checklist.
- PoC data handling: retention will be 30 days by default for logs; request/response payloads are retained only for debugging and will be removed at PoC end unless you request otherwise. We’ll send a short Data Processing Addendum for signatures.

I’ve attached the mutual action plan and the estimate spreadsheet. If that’s good, I’ll send a calendar invite for a kickoff with engineering.

Thanks all —
Marissa
